{{Quote|Right away, Governor. And may I say, you're looking particularly handsome today.|A sample of a BD-3000's "flattery programming"|<ref name="NEGTD" />}}
The '''BD-3000 luxury droid''', nicknamed the '''Bettie Bot''',<ref name="Episode Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode005.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Rookies}}</ref> was a versatile [[Service droid/Legends|luxury attendant droid]] built by [[LeisureMech Enterprises/Legends|LeisureMech Enterprises]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:BD_3000_1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A pair of BD-3000 luxury droids]]
The BD-3000 was modeled on an idealized [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body shape. It was programmed with a basic linguistic database, which made it capable of speaking over a million languages, and a respectable language processor, though its translation capabilities were not up to par with a dedicated [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]]. [[Droid/Legends|Droids]] of this series were intended to be used in a number of roles, being equipped with over 25 secondary functions, ranging from the technical ([[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] pilot) to the mundane (cook and tailor). In addition, BD-3000s were programmed with extensive personality matrices, allowing for a variety of droid personality profiles. Sophisticated [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] systems allowed the model to project a large number of sounds and voices, including presets described as "perky" and "sultry."

Onboard expansion slots allowed for user customization, with combat/[[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] upgrades being common (although not strictly authorized). The droid's main selling point, however, was not its well-rounded feature set and broad capabilities. Rather, it was the droid's remarkable aesthetics&mdash;its sculpted curvature, gleaming and very well defined torso, and gyro-stabilized gait that mimicked a provocative hip swing.<ref name="NEGTD" />

==History==
Half a century before the Clone Wars, LeisureMech Enterprises began producing the BD-3000. However, the company cut corners on the hardware and software for the sake of what critics called "a triumph of style over substance".<ref name="NEGTD" />

Because of their intended market, BD-3000 models were priced expensively, at roughly 25,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. Despite this price, sales were common, especially among the wealthy social "elite" of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] who regarded the shiny droids as status symbols. Many [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] were known to use the personal luxury droids as office aides, sometimes even bringing them to social functions, such as performances at the [[Galaxies Opera House/Legends|Galaxies Opera House]].

[[File:BD-3000_Hostage_Crisis.png|thumb|right|250px|A BD-3000 during the [[Senate hostage crisis/Legends|senate hostage crisis]].]]
The droids also found use in less-savory parts of society, where they functioned as escorts. Some were even fitted with fully-articulated [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]], capitalizing on the popularity of [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] females.<ref name="NEGTD" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a BD-3000 known as the [[Bettie-Bot VJ]] hosted a music program which broadcast across the galaxy. Her show was popular among the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], and she sometimes dedicated songs to particular units, such as the [[Mud Jumpers/Legends|Mud-Jumpers]] of the [[224th]].<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref> Another [[Unidentified BD-3000 luxury droid|luxury droid]] was used as a cloaked decoy for Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]].<ref name="Assassin">{{TCW|Assassin (episode)}}</ref>

After the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], BD-3000 droids become mostly unknown, thriving mainly in the criminal underworld where they often received radical modifications. [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] royalty used them as servers until the world's [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]].<ref name="Allegiance">[[Allegiance (novel)|''Allegiance'']]</ref> In the New Republic, surviving models worked odd jobs in the service industry.<ref name="NEGTD" />
